obligations.obligation: H. pipeline.py teardown: lazy import pattern correctness, foreign-collision containment, per-tile cost
obligations.finding: The teardown (`try: from region import shutdown_all_pools / except ImportError: pass / else: _shutdown_pools()`, pipeline.py:311-316) is correct for its purpose. Containment executed: (H1) a foreign top-level module `region` WITHOUT the attribute raises ImportError at from-import -> caught, no crash. (H2) a foreign `region` WITH a shutdown_all_pools attribute WOULD be executed per tile — real but repo-checkout-gated (the import can only resolve post-bootstrap in a repo; a wheel has no `region`), lowest-priority resolution, and requires a foreign package that shadows both the name and the attribute (note N3/R3; N8-41 vendoring removes it). (H3) in a repo-checkout row-A tile the teardown import itself loads region.region_pool even though no pool was ever created — the pipeline comment 'No-op unless this process dispatched a region route' is true of the SHUTDOWN CALL but not of the IMPORT; cost is one cached import per process plus a dict scan per tile (untimed by policy; trivial), pool threads are daemon so this is hygiene, not hang prevention (n840-1, consistent with the record). shutdown_all_pools itself is the repaired N8-14 implementation (closes live pools, untracks via _forget_pool, prunes) and the integration reuse/shutdown test passes against it.
